rawFindings.title: Auth error missing command_used property on error object
rawFindings.explanation: In RedisClient.prototype.do_auth, when auth fails and error occurs, the error passed to callback or emitted as 'error' event does not include the 'command_used' property as other errors do, which limits context for error handling.
rawFindings.suggestion: Add error.command_used = 'AUTH' before calling auth_callback or emitting 'error' event for failed auth.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: When client.auth with bad password is called without callback, 'error' event emitted lacks error.command_used property set to 'AUTH', hindering error identification.

rawFindings.title: Inconsistent error callback signature on auth failure
rawFindings.explanation: In RedisClient.prototype.do_auth, the auth_callback is called with only the error argument 'self.auth_callback(err)', inconsistent with node convention (error-first callback should be 'callback(err, result)').
rawFindings.suggestion: Change 'self.auth_callback(err)' to 'self.auth_callback(err, null)' or 'self.auth_callback(err)' with consistent callback semantics; standard practice is to always provide both err and result parameters.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Callback supplied to client.auth when invalid password causes auth failure only receives err argument, without result argument, which might confuse caller expecting two arguments.

rawFindings.title: return_error method missing command_used property set on error
rawFindings.explanation: The RedisClient.prototype.return_error method sets err.command_used = command_obj.command.toUpperCase(), which is correct and consistent with error handling enhancements.
rawFindings.suggestion: No change needed; this is adding useful information to error objects in return_error method.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Errors emitted from return_error now carry command_used property, improving error context for consumers.
